changes.evidence: The rotated note has separate le, modèle, complet, régulier and can. with its stop, then de K sur k and three dots. Modèle has the d/l stems; complet has its p descender and final t. The accent zone in modèle is crossed by the preceding prendre descender, so the preferred accented reading is locally doubtful. The masculine régulier ending does not contain the extra final e of H.
The first word has the tall looped l after a, then a small o and a detached low r-s run. No t begins it.
Between de and k is an open c-like loop joined to a low e return; it is a distinct word.
The d/e, sous and the long-descending g with groupes continuation are readable. Between sous and groupes is an empty gap, without a separate hyphen; C’s punctuation is not supplied.
After the overdrawn subgroup symbol, d is followed by a long compressed a-n run and a turned s ending before E_K.
A left parenthesis precedes the long p stem; the o/u/r strokes and separate compressed sa are visible before the line break to structure.

The two t stems in structure and its intervening c are visible; a two-dot colon follows. The next word has two uncrossed middle rises, favouring celle over cette; the segmentation remains uncertain. Two short parallel strokes at its right are retained as the written equals short form.

The raised word starts with a short i stroke/dot and a low n run before the tall t; there is no crossing x after an initial e. The remaining compressed letters favour intérieure. Its curved leader descends to the gap before the following word.

After rela-t and the dotted i region, the low final run favours an open o followed by n, but can also be read v-e. The word remains live beneath the insertion leader; preserve the lexical alternative.

The raised line reads et les, a clear N with lower s and separate prime, then qui with its q descender and final i dot. It stands above the cancelled initial qui and supplies the new subject before sont.

The small initial word is crossed, with a q-like head and descending return still visible; its remaining letters are obscured, so qui is retained doubtfully. Sont and the following j-descender, compressed ustemen run and terminal t return are live. The long return belongs to justement, not a cancellation of that word.
The second occurrence has separate sous and groupes, with a blank gap between their terminal/initial strokes. No detached hyphen appears in the gap.

A horizontal strike crosses the lower word. The initial low n/orm/a sequence and the l and t ascenders support normalisateurs, but the strike merges several middle and final strokes; the complete word is therefore retained with a local doubt. It is below the live sous groupes phrase.

The lower inertie has a cancellation crossing its letters. Décomposition is written distinctly above it, with the long p descender and the later t/i sequence. H retains the replacement but loses the cancelled word and raised state.
A separate looped de precedes the t-a-n-t-ô-t sequence; a detached curved accent is visible over the o position. The following mark is a comma.

The long curved stroke lies above l’extension, passing above the ordinary letter bodies and ending after the word. It is the attachment leader of de N_s′ sur, not a strike through l’extension. The word is live.

The raised first word is d plus a low e return, without a terminal s. The N, lower s-prime and sur are clear. The curved leader attaches the phrase after live l’extension, before the main-line des on the following line.
Ouvert is written below the inclusion sign; its initial oval o and u/v run, followed by the terminal r/t strokes, are separate from the main-line formula. It labels the inclusion.

Read with the full E_k(s) subset E_K formula: the target index has a straight stem and two sharp oblique arms. This differs from the rounded shoulder and return of the small k in the left k(s), and from E_k in the preceding parenthesis. The capital is kept literally.
A live s followed by u and a turned r stands after the inclusion target and before the parenthesis beginning sections. It is not crossed or joined to the lower ouvert label.
Following sections is a separate word with looped d and a low o-n-c run. The word is present before the quoted phrase on the next line.
After com and the long p descender, the small o is followed by the angular s and e-r return. There is no a-r sequence after p.

The old f remains visible as a long stem, descender and crossbar beneath separate dense cancellation strokes. The replacement is on a raised line; its leader curves down to the old subject position. Rat. has its detached abbreviation stop; the inserted formula reads f de U_K sur S. The underline beneath définie is separately visible and retained.
The word begins the next main baseline: the a/u run is followed by the two s strokes, dotted i and tall t stems. A separate accent stroke is present over the o position.

The main-line word begins with s and has no re-stric prefix before the t/i/on sequence. Partielle is written above it with distinct final l-l rises; a curved leader returns to the gap before obtenue, placing partielle after section.

The complete group term has U with nested angular K. The words after it are compressed au, then the looped d and e-s-s-u-s sequence of dessus, then de. No further section is written before E_k(s) on the next line.

The left end of the shaft curls upward into an open hook; the right end has two angular arrowhead arms. The target has a live sharp capital K, though it is retraced over a rounded earlier stroke. No separable earlier letter is invented.
The first word has a retraced e/s body and a separate tall t. It is followed by aussi directly, across a blank word gap; no elle with l ascenders is present there.
The strike passes through both words, but the initial e and two l ascenders in elle, followed by the e/s run and terminal t of est, remain visible.

After the left parenthesis and en, the two t uprights and compressed a-n run form tant. Its long crossing/return is continuous with the t strokes, without an independent cancellation. The next word has q, u, apostrophe, small o, descending p and a detached stop. There are no separately written à, près or action in this place.

The lower abbreviation has a strike through e-x-t. Its separate round stop lies to the right, beyond the cancellation endpoint, and remains uncrossed. Effective is raised above, with two distinct f stems and the later t/i/v/e sequence; its curved leader attaches before sur. The surviving stop therefore stands outside the deletion macro.

After pi and the right parenthesis is a crossed word with an open e and dense final s/t-region. The strike is real, but the ending is too overlapped to resolve C’s existing est doubt. H treats est as live.
The first cluster has n, an apostrophe and the compressed est ending. Autre is a separate low word with its crossed t, followed by que with the long q descender. It is not induite par.
The fine lower-left figures have a closed 9 head and long tail followed by an angular, cross-stroked 7. They are in another unnamed hand. H’s trailing editorial note is not manuscript text.

notes: Content summary: This leaf treats the residue fields k(s) of non-generic points as finite extensions of k and associates conjugacy classes of subgroups of E_K with points s of S. It identifies the N_s′ with the decomposition subgroups discussed in the prose, considers sections of their extensions over E_k(s), and composes such sections with a given section. For a rational section f of U_K over S defined at s, the author claims that the resulting partial section is of the first kind and, as an effective operation on pi, is the one defined by f(s) in U_s(k(s)). A slanted marginal note proposes taking S to be the canonical regular complete model of K over k. The page ends with the isolated continuation word Dans. Layout and source work: one main prose paragraph on nineteen principal baselines, an oblique upper-left marginal note and another-hand folio97 below left. No author page number, display, diagram or drawing was found. The whole and both supplied halves were each read once, including agreed words; thirty unique crops were saved and inspected. The margin crop was rotated clockwise 39 degrees; its original rectangle is retained in crop_boxes.json and the rotation in crop_rotations.json. All other crop boxes are in original pixels. State and punctuation decisions: l’extension is live. Its apparent cancellation in C is a curved insertion leader above the letters, attaching de N_s′ sur after the word. The lower ext has crossed letters but a separate uncrossed stop beyond the strike, hence deleted ext followed by a live stop and the raised effective. The long stroke in tant belongs to its t crossing/return, so en tant remains live. The cancelled est after pi remains doubtful. The cancelled initial qui and normalisateurs acquire local reading doubts because the strikes merge letters. The underline on définie is retained. Both sous groupes occurrences have empty gaps, without a written hyphen. Tantôt and aussitôt each have an actual accent stroke; the modèle accent is uncertain because the preceding descender enters that zone. The three dots after E_k and after marginal k are retained, as are the comma after the first parenthesis, the period after donnée and the final point before Dans. Notation cautions: the subgroup symbol has a triangular live-looking outline, top crossbar/upright and dense upper-right overdraw. This is covered by a whole-symbol Delta/I doubt; no earlier deleted letter is invented. Both disputed targets are literal capital K, supported by sharp branches and same-page contrasts with rounded lowercase k in k(s) and E_k. The lower target K is retraced over a rounded stroke, but a separate deleted k is not recoverable. The capital K readings may conflict with an expected common base in the proposed section construction; they are not normalized. Likewise the extra live sur after the inclusion is not omitted for grammar. The low initial letter in obtenue and the e/s body of est are retraced without a securely separable earlier word. A tiny isolated dot near the lower target K has no secure punctuation role and is not promoted to a formula symbol. The equals short form is preserved; the uncertain celle/cette segmentation is not replaced by a barred-m abbreviation on grammatical expectation. Mathematical scope: only source reading, attachment tracing and same-page notation comparisons were performed. No proof of the assertion about specialization, first-kind sections, conjugacy classes or effective actions was attempted or used to force a reading. The check_events list is therefore empty. H’s final comment about rapid writing is editorial, not source text.
